text:
Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest called it "one of the wildest and most chaotic games in recent" Sharks history, and we're not going to argue. Ten goals, four power-play goals, two comebacks, a first NHL goal, and a shootout that went five rounds before Mason Marchment ended it. San Jose won 6-5.

Utah looked in control early. Zac Jones, a defenseman, scored twice in the first period, and Mikhail Sergachev added a power-play goal in between, so the Mammoth led 3-1 after 20 minutes. The Sharks tied it with two goals six seconds apart early in the second, Adam Gaudette on the power play and Zack Ostapchuk right off the next shift. Jack McBain put Utah back in front, and it stayed 4-3 until Eric Pohlkamp, a rookie defenseman, scored his first NHL goal 5:23 into the third. Dmitry Orlov then scored on a slap shot that goes in about 3% of the time, the least likely goal of the night, and San Jose's win chance went from 48% to 85%. Barrett Hayton tipped in a power-play goal with 3:38 left and swung it right back.

Orlov finished with a goal and three assists, and San Jose's chances were better than even with him on the ice (1.61 expected goals for, 0.37 against). Yaroslav Askarov's biggest save came in overtime on Clayton Keller, a 22% chance that would have ended it. Neither goalie had a good night: Karel Vejmelka allowed five on 21 shots, about 1.8 more than they deserved, and Askarov five on 32.

On the chances it was a coin flip that leaned Utah (53% in our replays), and Utah owned the third period. But the Mammoth are without Logan Cooley, Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther, and they are now winless in five (0-2-3). San Jose plays Nashville tonight on short rest.
headline: Sharks survive ten goals and a shootout in Utah
